handoff: Review approve: MO3 session ownership does what gh-92 asks; every Wanted clause traced to tests (table in handoff). 3 findings, 0 blocking: auto runs with unknown session unprotected (accepted by MO3), callerSession matches Claude's PreToolUse only, misplaced doc comment in hook.ts.

findings.title: A run with no recorded agent session (auto launch before any hook) is not protected
findings.detail:
runAgentSession returns null when neither state.run nor the started receipt names a session (e.g. a headless/herdr auto launch), so foreignSessionRefusal and foreignFact let every session through, and hook.ts stamps a second session's facts with the run_id. The spec says 'A run belongs to the session that started it' without exception; MO3 as amended explicitly accepts it ('When either session is not known, nothing is refused'), and the handoff names it. The observed case (manual mode) is covered.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Follow-up issue: record the run's session from its first stamped hook fact (the launch's NORN_RUN) so an auto run gets an owner.

findings.title: callerSession matches only Claude's native 'PreToolUse'
findings.detail:
The exact-call match checks f.native === "PreToolUse"; gemini (BeforeTool) and opencode (tool.execute.before) never match and fall back to the latest session fact in the worktree, which with two live sessions can be the other session's (e.g. B's fact lands between A's pre-tool hook and A's `norn done`), refusing the owner. An adapter-specific name in cli, where the normalised event (tool_use) plus a pre/post distinction from the adapter would do.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Let the adapter say which native event is the pre-tool one (or record a phase on the fact), and match on that.

findings.title: decideBlock's doc comment now sits above foreignFact
findings.detail:
foreignFact was inserted between `/** A4 / MO4: block turn end only in … */` and decideBlock, so that comment documents nothing (two JSDoc blocks in a row above foreignFact).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Move foreignFact above the A4/MO4 comment.
